cells.tense: What the pattern does with the content stripped off is what you see now, with the pen.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Pick the thing you actually want most and turn your week toward it — one move, small enough to make before anyone else is up.
cells.core:
You take a thing apart and the parts show you how it works, and you put it back together differently. That is not just a way of thinking — you have used it. Knowing how something works underneath what it looks like changes what you do next, and anyone beside you can feel that.

The balance is not something to fix. It runs itself when you are looking at real things. Where it stalls is when a pattern is seen and then admired, not followed. There is a pull available to you now, though — toward something that wants doing. Pick the thing you actually want most, and turn toward it. See what a step feels like, and what you want to do about that.
cells.sheetLine: You see how it works, and that is where you are.
cells.verb: seeing how things work underneath what they look like
cells.place: where one pattern gets seen plain, free of the literal thing in front of you

cells.tense: The future is being mapped before it has happened, and the mapping has stopped ending.
cells.act: build the smallest structure that holds it
cells.ask: When the analysis has no end in sight, build the smallest container around it — a list, a time, a line — and call that done.
cells.core:
Pattern-seeing turns on itself when there is nothing to hold it. You look at one thing, then the thing it came from, then the thing that comes after, and the readiness for what might be next gets built before there is any sign of it. What was a clear eye on how things work looks worse when the light is off. Analysis without an end is not depth. It is waiting to be shown something and not letting it show.

There is still a way with this. Not more thinking. Put a wall around one piece of it: a few lines, a time and a place and a boundary. The wall is on what you will think about now, and it says when. You find out you can make things clear without having to finish seeing all of them.
cells.sheetLine: The pattern keeps unspooling because nothing is holding it.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door you have already walked through.
cells.act: learn how the people before you did it
cells.ask: Find somebody who knows more than you about a craft you care about, and watch how they do it — no money, no readiness needed, just the method.
cells.core:
Somewhere in your life there are plain things and you have kept them plain. No depths, no meanings, no larger shapes — just the facts on the surface, and no interest in what is underneath. That is not who you are. You have seen underneath before, and something in you closed that not because you asked it to.

Depth does not come back by trying to think deeper. It comes through other people, through the way a method has been taught and handed along. Find a skill you care about being better at, and watch how the people who know it actually work. The pattern of their way will be waiting in what they do, and your eye will remember.
cells.sheetLine: You are keeping everything at the surface on purpose.

cells.tense: You are reading the pattern in front of you and do not notice it is already yours.
cells.act: sit with someone in it without fixing it
cells.ask: Tell somebody one pattern you can see running in the situation, and stay in it with them, without making it better. This week, once, no fixing.
cells.core:
You see it — how a thing came to be, the shape underneath it — and your own account of it sounds like a report rather than something you are doing. You have no idea how a pattern you pointed out is holding you right now. That is not blindness. That is the part you do not believe is part of it.

What is asked is smaller than what you have already seen. Look at one pattern you see clearly, then find somebody who is inside the same kind of thing, and tell them what you see. Not so they can tell you whether you are right. Their honesty about how it lands can show you. Your own pattern can be plain in the space between that.
